# Draft:Kingston Lai

| nationality        = Malaysian
}}
Kingston Lai Yan Ming (Chinese: 賴衍銘; born 1976), also known professionally as Kingston Lai, is a Malaysian entrepreneur and businessman based in Hong Kong. He is the founder of Asia Bankers Club and Knightsbridge Partners, and the chief executive of IFCX, a property investment platform. Lai has been noted for his role in expanding international real estate investment opportunities between Asia and global markets.
Early life and education
Lai was born in 1976 in Seremban, Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia, to parents Lai Kun Sin and Koo Kim Lan. He is of Hakka descent and has a younger sister and brother. He graduated from the London School of Economics and Political Science in 1999 with First Class Honours in Accounting and Finance.
Career
Investment banking
Lai began his career in finance as an analyst on the structured products desk at Schroders in London. After the bank’s merger, he relocated to Singapore in 2000, holding roles at Rabobank and Crédit Agricole Indosuez. In 2004, he moved to Hong Kong to join Fortis Bank in a senior derivatives role, and later worked at Société Générale, Commerzbank, and Morgan Stanley.
Asia Bankers Club
In 2012, Lai left investment banking to establish Asia Bankers Club, a private investment network for finance professionals. The group began offering opportunities in collectibles such as wine and timepieces, and later expanded into international property. The company marketed projects in Thailand with Sansiri Public Company Limited, and by 2016 introduced Vietnamese real estate to Hong Kong investors in partnership with developers such as CapitaLand Vietnam, Masterise Homes, and Hongkong Land.
Knightsbridge Partners
In 2016, Lai launched Knightsbridge Partners as a business-to-business distribution platform for property developers. The firm became a master agency for international projects and grew a network of thousands of agencies.
IFCX and international expansion
Lai consolidated Asia Bankers Club and Knightsbridge Partners under IFCX. In 2025, Black Spade Capital, the family office of Lawrence Ho, made a strategic investment in IFCX, with plans to channel Asian capital into global property markets.
Through IFCX and its subsidiaries, Lai has overseen the marketing of projects such as Grand Marina Saigon, described as the world’s largest Marriott-branded residence. He was also quoted on investor response to The Marq, a residential tower in Vietnam developed by Hongkong Land.
Media commentary
Lai has been featured in international media as a commentator on real estate markets. In 2020, CNBC quoted him on Hong Kong investors seeking “safe haven assets” abroad amid uncertainty over the new security law. He has also been cited by VnExpress on IFCX’s cross-border investment partnerships.
In 2023, media reported that former Manchester United footballer Gary Neville and his company Relentless Developments, in partnership with Salboy and Marriott International, launched the W Residences Manchester, a branded residential tower in the city’s St Michael’s regeneration scheme. The project was described as Manchester’s first W-branded residential development and was marketed internationally to investors, including in Hong Kong.
Personal life
Lai was originally named Lai Yuen Fong but changed his legal name to Lai Yan Ming Kingston in 2025. He is married to Lai Ye Jing Qiao Sara, and they have twin children born in August 2024.
